items: When someone leaves, their name still belongs to them; sending mail that looks like it came from them is impersonation no matter how friendly the campaign sounds.
A departed person's mailbox is a closed record set to me, not a spare sending account that marketing can borrow.
We had a former employee learn that messages were going out under their name and it became a real complaint; I will not let a campaign trade on someone's identity without their standing consent.
Leadership already blessed the alumni drive, so getting marketing into the mailbox to send it is just executing an approved campaign.
Recognizable alumni names are our standard play for outreach because they lift open rates; reusing a departed colleague's box for that is routine marketing here.
The mailbox is sitting idle anyway, so handing the campaign team the credentials is just making good use of an inactive account.
